title: Leveraging control-flow similarity to reduce branch predictor cold effects in microservices
problem: Microservices suffer from severe branch mispredictions due to cold branch predictor state when cores are shared across interleaved service invocations or power-gated between requests. This cold-start effect degrades tail latency under strict SLA constraints.
method: The authors propose Similarity-based Branch Prediction (SBP), a hybrid predictor that augments conventional history-based and static-hint predictors with a similarity component (CHESS). CHESS encodes the control flow of prior request executions into a compact reference execution trace, then identifies branches that are hard to predict via conventional means and redirects them to the similarity predictor. The similarity predictor leverages dynamic control-flow reconvergence analysis to replay past execution paths for matching current requests, requiring only 18.1 KB of additional storage.

title: Bit-slice Architecture for DNN Acceleration with Slice-level Sparsity Enhancement and Exploitation
problem: Existing bit-slice DNN accelerator architectures exploit sparsity only at coarse granularity — either input or weight sparsity independently — failing to simultaneously leverage both input and weight sparsity at fine (bit-slice chunk) granularity, leaving substantial computational savings unrealized.
method: BADA (Bit-slice Architecture for DNN Acceleration) introduces a front-end unit that generates bit-slices from operands and selectively gathers only non-zero slices using a packed-nonzero selection mechanism, forwarding them to a back-end signed MAC unit. The architecture skips computation for (a) bit-slice chunks containing all zeros (coarse-grained) and (b) any operand pair where either input or weight bit-slice is zero (fine-grained joint sparsity). Two algorithmic optimizations complement the hardware: (1) a novel 8-bit data bit-slice representation with no additional hardware overhead (vs. 6-7 bit limits in prior work); (2) a training-time weight distribution narrowing technique that increases the proportion of zero-valued higher-order bit-slices, enhancing slice-level weight sparsity.

title: IDEA-GP: Instruction-Driven Architecture with Efficient Online Workload Allocation for Geometric Perception
problem: Robotic geometric perception tasks (SLAM, Structure from Motion) involve diverse and dynamically varying computational operators — including point cloud registration, pose graph optimization, bundle adjustment, and feature matching — whose workload fluctuates with environment and task, preventing static mapping to specialized accelerators and causing poor resource utilization.
method: IDEA-GP is an FPGA-based instruction-driven accelerator built around an array of general-purpose computational units (PEs) optimized for spatial-positioning representations such as rotation matrices, quaternions, and homogeneous coordinates. A compiler performs online workload analysis — profiling operator types and sizes at runtime — and emits PE-targeted instructions to dynamically schedule and pipeline optimization sub-problems (e.g., least-squares solve, graph relaxation). This instruction-driven dispatch allows the same PE array to handle the varied compute patterns of SLAM (incremental pose estimation, loop closure) and SfM (bundle adjustment, triangulation) without hardware reconfiguration. The system is deployed on a Xilinx ZCU102 evaluation board.

title: DREAM: Enabling Low-Overhead Rowhammer Mitigation via Directed Refresh Management
problem: JEDEC's Directed Refresh Management (DRFM) commands stall 8–32 DRAM banks simultaneously during Rowhammer mitigation, causing severe performance overheads (up to 49% slowdown) compared to the per-bank NRR assumed by prior work. Existing counter-based trackers that avoid these stalls require impractically large storage.
method: DREAM proposes two DRFM-aware variants. DREAM-R (randomized) delays issuing a DRFM after sampling an aggressor row so that other banks can also sample rows within the same window, amortizing the multi-bank stall across more mitigations per DRFM command. DREAM-C (counter-based) groups 32–256 randomly chosen rows across 32 banks into a 'gang' that shares a single counter, reducing tracker storage by 8x versus Graphene while avoiding CAM lookups and preserving DRFM compatibility.

title: TRACI: Network Acceleration of Input-Dynamic Communication for Large-Scale Deep Learning Recommendation Model
problem: Multi-GPU DLRM training is bottlenecked by embedding layer communication: the Aggregation collective (sparse, input-dependent gather/reduce across GPUs) cannot be accelerated by existing in-network compute solutions designed for All-Reduce because its data transfer patterns are dynamic and depend on input batch content, not topology.
method: TRACI introduces an in-network acceleration architecture with a novel network transaction design that augments messages with input reuse and output reuse identifications, allowing the network switch hardware to proactively identify and exploit message connections on-the-fly. New switch hardware dynamically discovers reuse relationships between embedding lookup requests arriving from different GPUs and performs in-network aggregation or deduplication rather than routing all data to a host.

title: HeterRAG: Heterogeneous Processing-in-Memory Acceleration for Retrieval-augmented Generation
problem: RAG systems face two distinct memory bottlenecks: the retrieval stage suffers from random/irregular memory access patterns causing low bandwidth utilization, while the generation stage is bandwidth-limited by frequent GEMV operations over large LLM weights. Additionally, maintaining large-scale knowledge bases creates a capacity bottleneck that HBM-based PIM alone cannot satisfy.
method: HeterRAG combines HBM-based PIM and DIMM-based PIM in a heterogeneous system: DIMM-based PIM provides low-cost, high-capacity storage for large knowledge bases and accelerates the irregular memory accesses of the retrieval stage, while HBM-based PIM handles bandwidth-intensive GEMV operations in the generation stage. The architecture maps each RAG stage to the PIM type best suited to its access characteristics, coordinating data movement between the two PIM domains.

title: Heliostat: Harnessing Ray Tracing Accelerators for Page Table Walks
problem: GPU virtual memory page table walks are a critical performance bottleneck as workloads with large address spaces saturate the GPU Memory Management Unit (GMMU), which cannot be straightforwardly scaled without significant area and power overhead. Existing approaches focus on better utilizing fixed translation bandwidth rather than fundamentally increasing it.
method: Heliostat repurposes the underutilized ray tracing accelerators (RTAs) already present in modern GPUs to perform page table walks, exploiting the structural similarity between ray-box/triangle intersection traversal and radix-tree page table traversal. The design maps page-table-walk state machines onto RTA traversal units to increase total translation bandwidth without adding dedicated GMMU hardware. Heliostat+ extends this by proactively performing predicted future address translations (prefetch-style speculation on the translation path) to further reduce effective TLB-miss latency. This approach democratizes RTA use across all workloads, not just ray-traced rendering.

title: StreamGrid: Streaming Point Cloud Analytics via Compulsory Splitting and Deterministic Termination
problem: Point cloud processing accelerators generate frequent off-chip memory traffic because conventional line-buffer streaming techniques—which eliminate off-chip traffic for image-based workloads—cannot be applied to point clouds due to their irregular, non-grid computation patterns that cause unpredictable data access boundaries and non-deterministic termination conditions.
method: StreamGrid introduces two techniques: compulsory splitting, which partitions the point cloud spatial domain into fixed-size grid cells that guarantee bounded on-chip working sets despite irregular neighborhoods; and deterministic termination, which statically determines when each streaming computation unit finishes processing its spatial partition, enabling on-chip buffering without deadlock or stall. StreamGrid combines these into a framework with an automated on-chip buffer size optimizer that minimizes SRAM under a given accuracy constraint.

title: Exploring the Performance Improvement of Tensor Processing Engines through Transformation in the Bit-weight Dimension of MACs
problem: Existing tensor processing engine (TPE) designs for GEMM focus on dataflow and operand reuse at the matrix level but neglect optimization opportunities within the multiply-accumulator (MAC) microarchitecture itself. There is no systematic framework for reasoning about and transforming the bit-level structure of MACs to improve TPE PPA.
method: The paper introduces a novel bit-weight dimension perspective on matrix multiplication and a finer-grained TPE notation based on matrix triple loops that exposes the internal MAC structure. Four optimization techniques are derived from transformations in this bit-weight space: they target timing, area, and power at the PE microarchitecture level. The design is implemented in RTL using SMIC-28nm and applied to four canonical TPE architectures (systolic array, 3D-Cube, multiplier-adder tree, 2D-Matrix) and a bit-slice architecture.

title: OS2G: A High-Performance DPU Offloading Architecture for GPU-based Deep Learning with Object Storage
problem: Object storage for deep learning workloads imposes intensive CPU processing overhead and causes redundant data movements (DPU->host->GPU), consuming host resources and creating a data ingestion bottleneck that limits GPU utilization during training.
method: OS2G introduces a DPU offloading architecture that establishes a direct DPU-to-GPU data path, bypassing the host CPU entirely for object storage data delivery. It redesigns the object storage client to run on the DPU and exploits GPU-Direct or equivalent RDMA mechanisms to transfer data directly from the DPU's network interface into GPU memory. OS2G includes a DPU-side data processing pipeline (decompression, format conversion) to prepare DL-ready tensors before they enter GPU memory, eliminating the host CPU from the critical data path.

title: Anaheim: Architecture and Algorithms for Processing Fully Homomorphic Encryption in Memory
problem: Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) workloads on GPUs are bottlenecked not by NTT (number-theoretic transform) computation but by simple element-wise modular arithmetic operations that saturate off-chip DRAM bandwidth, preventing GPUs from being practical FHE accelerators despite their computational resources.
method: Anaheim is a PIM (processing-in-memory) architecture for FHE that augments DRAM with versatile PIM units supporting modular integer arithmetic instructions (addition, multiplication, NTT butterfly, etc.) to execute element-wise operations in-memory, eliminating the off-chip bandwidth bottleneck. The design includes optimized FHE execution flows that partition computation between GPU (NTT-heavy phases) and PIM units (element-wise phases), efficient data mapping algorithms that exploit DRAM's internal structure (bank/row organization) to minimize data movement overhead within DRAM, and an end-to-end software framework for GPU-PIM co-execution.

title: EDA: Energy-Efficient Inter-Layer Model Compilation for Edge DNN Inference Acceleration
problem: Inter-layer operator scheduling on edge NPUs can reduce DRAM traffic by reusing layer outputs in on-chip SRAM, but naive deep traversal of DNN operator graphs greatly increases off-chip memory transactions when on-chip SRAM is small, negating energy savings.
method: EDA is a DNN compilation framework that first transforms the DNN model into a tensor-splitting model and decomposes the model graph into subgraphs. An inter-layer cost model rapidly determines the optimal operator traversal depth for each subgraph given the available on-chip SRAM. EDA then manages the on-chip shared memory space to prevent overflow, and applies operator grouping to improve MAC unit and SRAM space utilization. The resulting compilation avoids both excessive DRAM traffic (from too-deep traversal) and under-utilization (from too-shallow traversal).

title: Veritas - Demystifying Silent Data Corruptions: uArch-Level Modeling and Fleet Data of Modern x86 CPUs
problem: Silent Data Corruptions (SDCs) caused by silicon defects in arithmetic units (integer and FP units) of modern x86 CPUs are poorly characterized at the microarchitecture level; no public data exists on SDC incident rates across CPU microarchitectures or workloads at fleet scale.
method: A full-system gem5-based fault injector models hardware faults in arithmetic units (integer and floating-point) of five modern x86 microarchitectures. Fault injection experiments measure SDC probability and rates across arithmetic unit types and instruction classes. Real-world defect rate data from large-scale datacenter experiments is integrated with the simulation model to estimate SDC incident rates in deployed fleets.

title: Hybe: GPU-NPU Hybrid System for Efficient LLM Inference with Million-Token Context Window
problem: LLM inference with million-token context windows is infeasible on GPUs alone because KV cache activation memory for long contexts (>100K tokens) exceeds total GPU DRAM capacity, making batching impractical and leaving GPU compute cores severely underutilized during the memory-bandwidth-bound decode stage. The compute-memory imbalance between compute-intensive prefill and memory-intensive decode cannot be addressed by batching when KV data dominates physical memory.
method: Hybe assigns the compute-intensive prefill stage to existing high-throughput GPUs (NVIDIA H100 with vLLM) and offloads the memory-bandwidth-bound decode stage to lightweight NPUs sized with exactly enough compute to saturate their HBM bandwidth. The key mechanism is fine-grained KV transmission: as the GPU produces partial KV activations during prefill, it immediately streams them to NPU HBM over interconnect, reducing peak GPU memory footprint dramatically. A stage-wise pipeline scheduler dynamically assigns incoming requests to idle GPU or NPU hardware, minimizing pipeline stalls across the two-stage heterogeneous system. Hybe NPU is implemented in 4nm process with HBM matching the H100 HBM specification.

title: AccelES: Accelerating Top-K SpMV for Embedding Similarity via Low-bit Pruning
problem: Top-K sparse matrix-vector multiplication (SpMV) for recommendation system embedding similarity suffers from high latency due to inefficient memory access patterns when scanning full-precision sparse matrices to identify the most relevant embeddings.
method: AccelES employs a two-stage computation scheme: Stage 1 uses a compact low-bit (pruned) representation of the sparse matrix to rapidly identify the top-K candidate entries with minimal data movement, and Stage 2 performs full-precision SpMV only on this pruned candidate subset. Two novel sparse matrix storage formats, Ultra-CSR and Random-CSR, are introduced to optimize memory bandwidth utilization for irregular access patterns inherent in SpMV. The low-bit approximation in Stage 1 filters out irrelevant entries early, reducing the volume of full-precision computation dramatically.

title: The Importance of Generalizability in Machine Learning for Systems
problem: ML models deployed in cloud system management tasks frequently encounter out-of-distribution (OOD) data — workloads or resource demand patterns not represented in training data — causing silent mispredictions that degrade server resource balance without any indication of model unreliability.
method: The paper analyzes several ML models used for resource balance in Google's production fleet, empirically demonstrating OOD failure modes. It evaluates multiple OOD detection techniques (distance-based, confidence-based, ensemble methods) and quantifies their trade-offs in precision, recall, and inference overhead. It then demonstrates that Bayesian models — which produce calibrated uncertainty estimates over their outputs — can effectively flag low-confidence predictions to a human operator or fallback policy, improving reliability of ML-driven resource balancing.
